(and the matching "What not to add" bullet): the sentence states a product-support fact that the shipped project still contradicts, and the change reconciles neither side. `README.md` still lists SQLite and Postgres in its "Database URLs" table, its sixty-second quick start is built on the bundled SQLite demo, `docs/external/configuration.md` and `docs/external/getting-started.md` carry the same framing, and `sqllens init` still writes `sqlite:///./demo.db` as the default URL. claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: 2. `AGENTS.md`, the bullet "When a fix touches code with per-engine branches, change the MySQL branch only": applied literally, this leaves the fail-closed unknown-dialect path behind on a future safety fix. In `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` the unknown-dialect fallbacks are built from the per-dialect tables: `_DENIED_UNION` is the union of every dialect's denylist and is what `_denied_funcs` returns when the dialect is unknown or `None`, and `_ALL_CATALOG_SCHEMAS` / `_ALL_CATALOG_NAME_PREFIXES` are built the same way from `_CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT`. A hole fixed in the MySQL entry alone therefore stays open for the unknown-dialect case, which is the one the file documents as fail-closed. An exception for the shared fail-closed unions in `safety/` would keep the rule and the guard pointing the same way. (raised by 1/4 agents)
